title: Joint participant grouping and solvability in complete subset accounts
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. An owned Liber abbaci passage uses the same four totals in a uniquely soluble triple-subset problem and an explicitly impossible adjacent-pair problem, then announces a changed amount and a non-unique solution family. This constrains participant grouping and argument status together; no fixed source-count writer, numeral code or target owner is supplied.

design.mechanism: Whole-account interpretation with globally shared participant identity, subset-sum meaning, explicit case boundaries, and distinct assertions of solution, impossibility and free choice. Grouping and reference may be learned jointly; no old glosses or per-occurrence fresh holdings.
design.unit: The two complete four-man source problems, including the negative case, explicit revised case, explanations, checks and both owned result tables. No fixed target paragraph/field count.

source.boundary: Qvatuor homines sunt through ergo quartus habet denarios20; before Item sunt quinque homines. Full operative inventory in sealed dossier, not a diplomatic Latin transcription.

design.prediction: Same four totals under triple incidence determine one solution, while adjacent-pair incidence makes them inconsistent. Corrected pair incidence retains a degree of freedom; a unique-answer claim would be false. Solvability status must be bound by shared writing, not selected after a contradiction.
design.source_only_verification: PASS: historical triple equations and total; all28 nonnegative pair solutions and printed t10; generated triple/pair paths and contradiction. No target computation.
